problem: The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)={e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ about $x=0$ is
worked_solution:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!} \\  & =f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)x+{f}^{″}(0)\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{f}^{‴}(0)\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to compute $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & f(0) & ={e}^{-0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =-{e}^{-0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0-{e}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡0=-1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =2{e}^{-0}\operatorname{sin}⁡0=0 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =-2{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(0) & =-2{e}^{-0}\operatorname{sin}⁡0+2{e}^{-0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0=2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ ${f}^{″}(0),$ and ${f}^{‴}(0)$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =1+(-1)\cdot x+0\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+(2)\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{6} \\  & =1-x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
